findings.explanation: google_sourcerepo_repository.pike wires service_account_email = google_service_account.pike.email into its pubsub_configs, but no google_pubsub_topic_iam_member or google_pubsub_topic_iam_binding in the module grants that SA roles/pubsub.publisher on google_pubsub_topic.pike. Without this grant, Cloud Source Repositories cannot deliver notification messages, silently breaking any CI/CD pipelines or security-scan triggers that depend on commit events. A rules engine cannot detect this three-resource composition gap (CSR → SA → topic with the IAM grant missing).
findings.title: Service account in CSR pubsub_configs has no roles/pubsub.publisher IAM binding on the topic

findings.explanation: variables.tf:11 declares variable 'key' as type = string, but google_pubsub_topic.tf:3 accesses var.key.id (object-attribute notation on a string, which Terraform rejects). The example at example/examplea/module.cloudsource.tf:5 passes the full google_kms_crypto_key resource object, which Terraform will also reject against a string-typed variable. The practical result is that kms_key_name on the Pub/Sub topic cannot resolve correctly: callers who pass a plain string get a plan error on .id access; callers who pass an object get a type-constraint rejection. CMEK encryption is effectively non-functional as written.
findings.title: Variable 'key' declared as string but used as object — CMEK configuration is broken

findings.explanation: outputs.tf:2 exports value = google_sourcerepo_repository.example, but the only google_sourcerepo_repository declared in this module is named 'pike' (google_sourcerepo_repository.example.tf:1). Terraform will abort with 'Reference to undeclared resource' on every plan, making the module entirely non-functional for callers.
findings.title: outputs.tf references non-existent resource google_sourcerepo_repository.example (resource is named .pike)

suggested_policies.rationale: google_sourcerepo_repository has zero deterministic rule coverage. When pubsub_configs is present and service_account_email is omitted, GCP defaults to the Cloud Source Repositories service agent, which may hold broader permissions on the Pub/Sub topic than a dedicated least-privilege SA. Requiring an explicit service_account_email is a concrete, attribute-level check expressible with the current DSL.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_001
name: Cloud Source Repository Pub/Sub configs must specify an explicit service account
principle: identity-and-access
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  When google_sourcerepo_repository configures pubsub_configs without an explicit
  service_account_email, GCP uses the Cloud Source Repositories service agent.
  A dedicated, explicitly specified service account enforces least privilege for
  repository event notifications and makes the IAM grant auditable and reviewable.
remediation: |
  Add service_account_email to all pubsub_configs blocks pointing at a
  dedicated least-privilege service account:

  resource "google_sourcerepo_repository" "example" {
    pubsub_configs {
      topic                 = google_pubsub_topic.notifications.id
      message_format        = "JSON"
      service_account_email = google_service_account.csr_notifier.email
    }
  }
resources:
  google_sourcerepo_repository:
    path: pubsub_configs.service_account_email
    not_null: true
